recovery.implementation: Idle Endpoint operations execute on the calling thread. Only contended operations allocate a Future and enter the asynchronous queue. The hot Prefill capacity query avoids allocating a captured callback on the idle path; the same CAS ownership, record checks and retirement ordering remain in effect.
unchanged_preexisting_checks_not_rerun: ProjectionPerformanceTest (120 caller-thread bytes versus 96-byte limit in both original versions)

The complete functional reactor ran with the caller-execution change; the final Prefill callback-allocation edit was subsequently covered by 138 targeted contract tests and the remote microbenchmarks/E2E matrix.

changes: Encoder captures engine snapshot and local pending tokens together, then traverses immutable engine tasks outside the lock.
Encoder prepares request token metadata before admission; capacity check and insertion remain atomic.
Encoder retirement detaches its request map while locked and constructs notifications outside.
Decode captures same-version priority totals while locked, builds occupancy objects outside, and validates routing identity before cache publication.
Decode copies immutable heartbeat evidence lists after releasing the lock.

Baseline third-round BATCH 3K case failed with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED receiving request limit reached; its 10K measurement completed. Failure retained.
Benchmark uses a fixed uploaded snapshot. Concurrent scheduler and registry edits in the shared workspace after snapshot upload are excluded.
A shared-target test run encountered missing class files during concurrent Maven builds; isolated snapshot rerun passed 244 tests.

changes: Production lock callbacks replaced by direct lock/try/finally/unlock in endpoints and their scheduler callers.
Early unsuccessful returns release the lock in finally and do not emit capacity notifications.
Existing lock-external calculations and notifications preserved.
Lock fixture helpers moved from WorkerEndpoint production API into EndpointTestSupport test code.

changes: WorkerEndpoint.stateLock() is package-private; caller-locked Prefill methods are no longer public.
Scheduler and Dispatcher use Endpoint atomic APIs for queue-version checks, exact removal and delivery commit.
Queue policy is read from Endpoint bound settings rather than passed by Scheduler.
Scheduler waitLock owns waiting decisions, listener replacement and stop ownership; late decisions cannot resubscribe after stop.
Capacity subscriptions precede resource checks; subscription changes and request notifications do not borrow Endpoint locks.
added_contract_tests: Public API does not expose stateLock or caller-locked methods.
Queue business APIs validate exact identity, versions and expiry without caller locking.
Slow capacity subscription does not prevent Endpoint queue access; stop removes the listener and late waits cannot reinstall it.
Capacity release during subscription is not lost.

changes: Encoder status reconciliation visits local tracked requests, updates records and publishes status CAS under one lock; list allocation and defensive copy are outside.
Prefill admission blocker probe runs outside Endpoint lock and retries when the captured version changes.

Encoder route commit and Decode ownership lookup no longer wait for Endpoint locks while holding the request Context monitor.
